title: packages: an admin cannot disable a type:module sub-package of an installed app (422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED), and a disabled package's nav contributions stay in the app
body:
coordinator#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV5XwfXsVDMWfbUvBv

Filing gate: ③ ordered by the maintainer. Ruling thread, 2026-10-30, quoted verbatim (not translated):
> 2026-10-29 14:48Z: 暂时不考虑夸仓的这种。大包 + 设置里启用模块 你继续帮我调研分析。
> 2026-10-30 13:05Z: 同意
> 2026-10-30 13:07Z (on the optional organization-scope step): 可选第三步：组织级范围。不需要

The 13:05Z 「同意」 answers the analysis "the customer always installs one suite, and enables modules in settings" (project analysis of 2026-10-29, read on origin/main `eef83734`): plan A (platform-level hard switch), with the three defaults: (1) the customer's own admin switches modules on and off; (2) scope stays per environment, as today; (3) "disabled" has exactly ONE meaning = hidden + refused on the data plane + data kept. Organization-level scope: ruled not needed (13:07Z) — no card, no backlog entry.

Business reason: a suite (HotCRM) ships as ONE artifact with several `type: module` packages (ADR-0019 D3, ADR-0130 D2/D6). A customer who does not use a module wants it gone from their apps, and today nobody can do that: the disable door refuses every installed or code-booted package, so a suite module can never be switched off. Without this, "enable modules in settings" has no platform mechanism, and suites are pushed back toward separate artifacts (cross-repo dependencies, ruled deferred on #25805).
Reader who acts: the server lane (runtime + objectql), one PR; the `docs/adr/**` line is Tier H (maintainer approves).
Dedupe (open AND closed): semantic searches "disable module sub-package installed app WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED", "suite module enable disable nav contributions disabled package": 3 hits (#24813, #24062, #24030), all closed and about OTHER doors of the same gate; #7560 is the gate this card narrows. 0 open duplicates.

Back-link: #7560 (the gate), #25805 (ruled D) · ⛔ Not a claim.

## Today (origin/main `b6c2ed9c`)

- `PATCH /api/v1/packages/:id/disable` calls `requireWritablePackage(deps, qlService, id, 'disable')` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` ~L1723, function at L569) before `registry.disablePackage`. The predicate `isWritablePackage` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts` L73-85) answers read-only for a booted code package (`engine.manifests`) and for manifest `scope` `system` / `cloud`. So every module of an installed or code-loaded suite answers 422 `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED`. `PATCH …/enable` has no such gate.
- Once a package IS disabled, the platform already does the rest: lists hide its items (objectql `registry.ts` ~L6190-6200, protocol list predicate), by-name and data-plane reads answer 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, bound actions are withheld (#24400), the security catalog skips it, state persists per environment (`packages/runtime/src/package-state-store.ts`), reinstall keeps it (#18877).
- `applyNavContributions` (objectql `registry.ts` L6807) folds every registered contribution into the app; contributions are registered with their `packageId` (`registerAppNavContribution`, L6772) but the fold does not look at whether that package is disabled (read from source, not measured).
- Record-triggered flows on a disabled package's objects: not measured. service-automation only handles disabled PACKAGED SUBFLOWS today (#25222 guards).
- The row's served verdict `writable` (`withWritableVerdict`, packages.ts ~L766; spec `packages/spec/src/api/package-api-assembled.zod.ts` L155-166) is what the Console reads to offer Disable (`PackagesPage.tsx` L1054: `writable || !enabled`).

## Expected

1. **Disable door.** A package may be disabled by an admin with `manage_metadata` when it is `manifest.type: 'module'` AND it belongs to an installed `type: 'app'` package (same artifact / same namespace — the dev MEASURES which tie the registry actually carries for a suite installed both ways, marketplace install and code boot, and pins both). Everything else keeps answering 422 `WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` exactly as today: the app package itself, platform packages, `plugin` / `driver` / other types, and a module whose app is not installed. The exemption covers DISABLE only: edit, publish, revert, delete, overwrite stay refused on the module (it is still read-only for authoring, ADR-0070 D2).
2. **Nav.** `applyNavContributions` drops contributions whose `packageId` is disabled, on every read path that folds them (registry helpers and the protocol `app` read). Re-enable restores them.
3. **Flows.** Record-change triggers bound to a disabled package's objects: the dev measures first; if they still fire, they stop while the package is disabled and resume on enable, in this PR. If they already stop, a pin only.
4. **Served verdict.** The Console must not re-derive the rule (#8146: one answer to the question). The row carries the server's answer to "may this package be disabled here?" next to `writable`. If that needs a new key in `package-api-assembled.zod.ts`, that key is a spec-lane edit: report it as a fork / Seam before writing it, ⛔ do not overload `writable` (it means "may author into", and stays false for a module).
5. **Red tests first**: module of an installed app disables (200) and its objects 404 `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`, its nav items gone; re-enable restores both; app package, platform package, plugin, and an orphan module still 422; disable survives restart (state file).
6. **ADR-0070 D2**: one addendum line — "a `type: module` sub-package of an installed app may be disabled (not authored into) by an admin; ruling 2026-10-30". `docs/adr/**` is Tier H: governed PR, the maintainer approves.

## Not in scope (ruled)

- Organization-level scope (per org instead of per environment): Sales 2026-10-30 13:07Z 「不需要」.
- Plan B (app-level soft switch: a settings toggle that only hides menus) and plan C (license / plan driven): not taken.
- A second, weaker "hide menu only" disable level: not taken (one meaning only).
- Cross-repo app dependencies: #25805 ruled D (deferred).

## Linked

- Console half: the ui card filed alongside this one (the existing Packages page gets the toggle for these rows), `Blocked-by:` this card.
- HotCRM: hotcrm#2270 (modules organised inside ONE artifact, each a `type: module` package) is still the premise on the app side; hotcrm#2271 (revenue as a standalone artifact) is shelved by this direction. Neither card is edited here.
